Breakfast. Travel from Cusco to Puno on a Turismo Avalos sightseeing bus, with stops at historic sites and mountain villages along the way.

In Andahuaylillas, visit the Church of San Pedro Apóstol. Its murals, carved altars and colonial decoration have earned it the nickname “the Sistine Chapel of South America.” The next stop is Raqchi, where you will see the remains of the Temple of Viracocha, dwellings and storehouses in the Inca complex.

Stop for lunch in Sicuani. At La Raya Pass, the highest point on the road at about 4,300–4,400 m, take in views of the mountains and Andean plateaus and browse a small craft market. In Pucará, learn about the legacy of the pre-Inca culture of the same name.

The bus arrives in Puno at approximately 18:00. Transfer to the 4-star Casona Plaza or a similar hotel for your stay.

You can take the Titicaca Train instead of the bus. The supplement is $295 per person. The train runs on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, subject to the operator’s timetable.

The railway crosses the high Andes, passing through plateaus and valleys. The train has a dining car, a bar car and a panoramic observation car. At La Raya, a stop at over 4,300 m offers views of the mountain peaks and plains.

A three-course lunch of a starter, main course and dessert is included. Arrive in Puno at about 19:00, then transfer to the hotel for your stay.
